initial_japanese_execution.first_echelon: approximately six division-equivalents: 3d/13th/40th/68th/116th plus selected 27th/37th elements by axis
initial_japanese_execution.second_echelon: 34th/58th/64th and remaining 27th/37th elements move behind, secure flanks/roads and preserve the ammunition/bridge clock rather than all ten divisions consuming the same routes at once.
initial_japanese_execution.60th: theater reserve; not committed in opening 72 hours.
initial_japanese_execution.doctrine: Use artillery/engineer preparation, bypass or turn selected strongpoints, keep road/river repair close behind, and do not turn every Chinese rearguard into a prestige frontal battle.

daily_outline.result: Main axes break into the first northern-Hunan delay belt. Local crossings and demolitions slow some columns, but Japanese engineer/artillery package keeps multiple axes moving. Working main-axis depth 10-22 km from start positions by night.

Chinese main formations continue planned elastic withdrawal while rearguards fight bridge/river/hill positions. 14AF/CACW attacks exposed movement and Yueyang-area logistics; Japanese fighter/AA cover prevents a transport collapse. Main-axis depth 18-34 km.

First belt is being unhinged rather than annihilated. Main Chinese field formations preserve most heavy-command core southward. Japanese leading axes reach roughly 28-48 km from opening line; Changsha is not captured or directly stormed. Forward logistics remain coherent.

ground_losses_28_30Apr.interpretation: Initial exchange favors Japan but is not an annihilation. Chinese Five-Go learning converts part of the expected loss into orderly space-for-time withdrawal; Japanese v048 hardware/process gains improve local exchange without producing magical breakthrough speed.

air_opening.primary_effect: Counterair, airfield pressure and LOC interdiction shape movement and repair tempo. No side destroys the opposing air arm in the opening three days.

logistics_30Apr.note: Opening consumption, losses and temporary vehicle damage are charged; nightly rear feed continues. Stock remains above the minimum for continuation of Phase A but is not sufficient proof for automatic Hengyang continuation.

next_gate: Continue early-May northern-Hunan/Miluo-Liuyang approach. Recompute Chinese reserve placement, Japanese daily supply and 14AF sortie/fuel cost before assigning Changsha fall date. Hengyang remains closed.
